memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Now hurry back to my father and say to him, "This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; don't delay. You shall live in the region of Goshen and be near me—you, your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and all you have."'" — Gen 45:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Feel the urgency in Joseph's words. Hurry. Don't delay. Come down to me. Twenty years of separation are ending, and he cannot bear another day of it.

And notice the heart of the invitation: "be near me." That is what Joseph actually wants. Not their gratitude, not their service, not repayment. Nearness. He has power, wealth and position, and none of it means anything without his family beside him.

There is a message from God to us in that. Everything He has done — every promise, every provision, every act of rescue — has this at its centre: that we would be near Him. He did not save us primarily to make us useful. He saved us to bring us home. Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, "to bring you to God" (1 Pet 3:18). That is the destination.

Joseph could offer his family the best land in Egypt because of the position he held. Our Lord offers us a place with Him because of the position He now holds at the Father's right hand, and He has gone ahead to prepare a place for us (Jn 14:2-3).

The invitation is urgent, and it is warm. Come. Don't delay. Be near Me.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of salvation mainly as being forgiven, or as being brought near to God?
2. What is delaying you from drawing closer to Him?
3. Who in your life needs to hear an invitation rather than an argument?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You saved me to bring me near, not just to make me useful. Draw me close today, and take away whatever keeps me delaying. Amen.
